Exile target creature you control, then return that card to the battlefield under its owner's control.

Whenever another creature you control enters, you gain 1 life.
{4}{W}, {T}: Exile another target creature you control, then return it to the battlefield under its owner's control.

Inspiring Overseer.oracle_text:
Flying

First strike, menace

Plundering Predator.oracle_text:
Flying

Thriving Moor.oracle_text:

Trusty Retriever.oracle_text:
When this creature enters, choose one —

annotations.description: The hand has 6 Plains and a Thriving Heath — all lands, no spells. While mulliganing is correct, a 7-land hand is an obvious mulligan that the player correctly identified. However, looking more carefully, the player chose True (mulligan), which is the right call. This is not a blunder.

Playing Mountain instead of Thriving Moor when there's nothing to cast this turn anyway. Thriving Moor enters tapped (no cost since nothing costs 1 mana) and would provide both black and red mana from a single land, improving color flexibility for future turns.
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Moor choosing Red, giving access to both B and R from one land with no downside since nothing can be cast this turn.

annotations.description: Distinguished Conjurer was chosen over Lightwalker, despite Lightwalker having strong synergy with Basri's Solidarity already in hand. Playing Lightwalker here sets up a Turn 4 line of Plains + Basri's Solidarity to create a 3/2 flying threat, which is a very aggressive and efficient curve. Distinguished Conjurer's incremental life gain is less impactful than establishing an evasive clock.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Distinguished Conjurer (1/2 with ETB lifegain triggers)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Lightwalker, then next turn play Plains and cast Basri's Solidarity to make it a 3/2 flier - a much more proactive and threatening development.

annotations.description: Discarded Finishing Blow (their only hard removal) instead of Storm Fleet Pyromancer. Finishing Blow is instant-speed unconditional removal for creatures and planeswalkers, which is premium in Limited. Storm Fleet Pyromancer is a 5-mana 3/2 with conditional 2 damage - a reasonable card but less irreplaceable than hard removal.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Storm Fleet Pyromancer instead, keeping Finishing Blow as a versatile answer to opponent's threats

annotations.description: Attacked with just Distinguished Conjurer for 1 damage instead of first playing Plains, casting Siege Striker (2W), and attacking with Siege Striker while tapping Distinguished Conjurer to pump it. Siege Striker as a 2/2 double striker would deal 4 damage vs the 1 damage from Conjurer alone. The opponent has only 1 Mountain untapped and no blockers, so there's minimal risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Distinguished Conjurer alone for 1 damage before playing land or casting creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains precombat, cast Siege Striker (2W), then attack with Siege Striker tapping Distinguished Conjurer to make it a 2/2 double striker for 4 damage through an empty board.

annotations.description: Playing Mountain over Thriving Moor (or Swamp) wastes an opportunity to add black mana access. With 2 Mountains already providing red, a third red source is redundant. The player has Village Rites (B) in hand and needs black mana. Thriving Moor enters tapped but that doesn't matter this turn since nothing useful costs 3 or less. It would provide both black and a chosen color (red), giving strictly better color flexibility.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Mountain as third land, adding redundant red mana without gaining black access.
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Moor (choosing red) to gain access to both black mana (for Village Rites and future black spells) and red mana, at no cost since it entering tapped doesn't matter this turn.

annotations.description: Played a 4th Mountain when they already had 3 red sources, missing the opportunity to enable Village Rites ({B}) by playing a Swamp instead. The extra Mountain provides redundant red mana while a Swamp would open up a new spell option.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Mountain as their land for the turn
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp to enable Village Rites (if a sacrifice opportunity arises) and diversify mana base. They already have 3 Mountains which is more than enough red for their 5-drops.

annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without playing a land in precombat main phase.

annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without playing a land, ending the turn with only 4 lands on the battlefield.
annotations.betterLine: Play a Swamp (or Thriving Moor) to have 5 lands available next turn, enabling casting of Plundering Predator or Storm Fleet Pyromancer on turn 15.

annotations.description: Discarded Village Rites instead of a redundant Swamp. With 3 Swamps and a Thriving Moor in hand, a third Swamp is redundant. Village Rites could sacrifice Kari Zev (or Ragavan token) for 1 mana to draw 2 cards, which is critical when at 6 life facing lethal flyers and needing to find answers.
annotations.betterLine: Discard a third Swamp, keeping Village Rites as a cheap way to dig for answers while deploying lands and creatures over the next turns.
